name: ci-failure-detective
description: Tells you why a CI run failed. Give it a failed run, a pull request whose checks failed, or "the latest failure on main in owner/repo": it reads the failing job's log, checks the same job's recent run history, and gives one verdict: REAL (the likely culprit commit and author, with the changed lines the failure points at), FLAKY ("has failed 4 of the last 20 runs, and passed on a rerun"), or INFRA (runner, disk, network), with the log excerpt and a suggested fix when one is obvious. Counts, culprit and flakiness are computed in code, never guessed. After you approve the exact text it can comment the verdict on the pull request or open a flaky-test issue. On demand in chat; it never re-runs, reverts or pushes anything.

skills.name: CI failure verdict
skills.description: Why a CI run or a pull request's checks failed: a REAL / FLAKY / INFRA verdict with the culprit commit or the k-of-n flake rate, the log excerpt and a suggested fix; then a pull request comment or a flaky-test issue, written only after you approve the exact text.
examples: Why did CI fail on PR 123 in acme/shop?
What broke the latest failure on main in acme/shop?
